name.text: PROTOTYPE: Parsons — show minimum value (completing the square)

questiontext.text:
Show that the minimum value of \(x^2 + {@b@}x + {@c@}\) is \({@qval@}\), and state the value of \(x\) at which this minimum occurs.

Arrange the steps of the proof in the correct order.

[[parsons input="ans1"]] {"steps": {# parsons_encode(proof_steps) #}, "headers": ["Your proof:"], "available_header": ["Drag from here:"]} [[/parsons]]

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]]

generalfeedback.text:
Proof:

We complete the square on \({@quad_expr@}\).

Half the coefficient of \(x\) is \({@half_b@}\), so \({@x^2 + b*x@} = {@(x + half_b)^2 - bsq@}\).

Therefore \({@quad_expr@} = {@(x + half_b)^2 - bsq@} + {@c@} = {@csq_expr@}\).

Since \({@csq_inner@} \geq 0\) for all \(x\), the minimum value of the expression is \({@qval@}\).

This minimum occurs when \({@csq_inner@} = 0\), i.e. when \(x = {@-half_b@}\).
